rationale: mpeg2dec is a hot-loop media decoder (IDCT, motion compensation, VLC parsing) where runtime overhead is the dominant constraint, so the weight table favors low-cost passes and throttles expensive ones. SUB gets the highest weights because instruction substitution is cheap in both time and space yet strongly obscures the decoder's dense fixed-point arithmetic (DCT coefficients, rounding constants), making it the best security-per-overhead pass for this workload. BCF is favored moderately — it resists static analysis of the decode dispatch loops at acceptable cost — while its high SizeCost weight discourages applying it to every function, concentrating it where features indicate branch-heavy code. FLA is deliberately de-weighted on RuntimeCost: control-flow flattening routinely halves throughput in tight decode loops, so it should only trigger where runtime features are cool (setup, error handling), with a modest CorrectnessRisk weight reflecting its known interaction with switch/loop restructuring. IBR, ICALL, and IGV are kept at moderate levels as cheap indirection layers that harden call/target recovery for tools like static disassemblers, but ICALL is tempered because indirect calls hurt branch prediction in the decode hot path. SPLIT is enabled with low SecurityGain/Security emphasis but high Runtime/Size acceptance since it mainly amplifies FLA/BCF effectiveness at negligible cost; it is harmless to keep in the pool. Overall the table biases the feature-driven selector toward arithmetic obfuscation and controlled bogus-flow insertion while keeping flattening and call/graph indirection selective, preserving decoder throughput and correctness.
